question: What is the main goal of medical services for children with special needs?

options.A: Providing specialized health and growth support for impaired children
options.B: Performing major surgeries for birth defects only
options.D: Giving routine vaccines in local health clinics

explanation: Special services focus on managing long-term physical, mental, or sensory challenges rather than standard short-term pediatric care. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why do children with special needs require care beyond regular pediatric medicine?

options.A: Their conditions involve complex, long-term health and developmental needs
options.B: Standard pediatric drugs do not work well in Nigeria
options.C: Routine vaccines cannot protect children with physical disabilities
options.D: Hospitals require separate wards for all chronic illnesses

explanation: Birth defects and long-term conditions require a mix of health, social, and developmental support over a long period. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h1)

question: Which health worker is often the first to notice developmental delays during regular visits?

options.A: The orthopedic surgeon on hospital rounds
options.B: The clinic nurse during immunization or wellness visits
options.C: The hospital pharmacist giving out syrups
options.D: The lab scientist testing blood samples

explanation: Nurses who handle routine clinic and immunization visits are usually the ones who spot early signs of delayed growth. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h2)

question: A 12-month-old baby is not babbling or saying any single words. What does this mean?

options.B: A common speech delay in baby boys
options.C: A normal delay that will fix itself
options.D: A warning sign that needs a formal check-up

explanation: Not babbling or talking by one year old is a classic red flag that means the child needs a closer evaluation. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h2)

question: What is the main job of a physiotherapist on a special needs team?

options.A: Helping families find financial aid and charities
options.B: Managing movement, body strength, and muscle stiffness

explanation: Physiotherapists focus on helping children improve their physical movement, muscle strength, and overall mobility. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why is regular communication among different team members so important?

options.A: It removes the need for parents to help plan care
options.B: It stops conflicting medical advice and uncoordinated care
options.C: It reduces the yearly number of hospital visits
options.D: It guarantees a complete cure for all disorders

explanation: Teamwork ensures that all health workers pull in the same direction without confusing the family. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which therapy helps children learn daily tasks like dressing and eating?
explanation: Occupational therapy helps individuals gain independence in practical, everyday life activities. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h4)

question: A child with cerebral palsy has tight heel cords that make walking hard. What is the best step?

options.B: Complete bed rest to protect the joints
options.C: Surgical removal of the lower leg muscles
options.D: Stretching exercises and splints managed by a physiotherapist

explanation: Physiotherapists use targeted stretching and splints to handle tight joints and help children move better. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the main goal of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR) programs?

options.B: Putting all complex children's surgeries in big city hospitals
options.C: Bringing rehab services closer to rural families and local towns
options.D: Providing free international trips for surgery

explanation: CBR programs bring care directly to local areas so families do not have to travel far to find help. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h5)

question: Why are community support groups helpful for parents of special children in Nigeria?

options.A: They replace the need to see doctors and nurses
options.B: They guarantee government jobs for the child later
options.C: They reduce loneliness and help soften the blow of social stigma
options.D: They provide signed contracts for free lifelong hospital care

explanation: Support groups connect families facing similar challenges, offering emotional backing against societal stigma. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is the main idea behind family-centered care in children's nursing?

options.A: Seeing the family as an active partner in the child's care
options.B: Leaving all daily care choices to the doctors
options.C: Limiting parents to afternoon visiting hours only
options.D: Focusing only on the physical disease

explanation: Family-centered care works best when health workers and family members team up together. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h6)

question: Why should nurses pay attention to how brothers and sisters feel in a family with a special child?

options.A: Siblings must be trained to replace physical therapists
options.B: Other children in the family can feel left out and burnt out
options.C: Sibling jealousy directly causes birth defects
options.D: Siblings are legally required to take over guardianship

explanation: Because a special child needs a lot of attention, other siblings can sometimes feel emotionally neglected. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge for special needs services in Nigeria?

options.A: Paying out-of-pocket, which puts heavy stress on families
options.B: Lack of money for disability-friendly buildings
options.C: Too many special pediatric rehab centers
options.D: Severe shortages of trained children's therapists

explanation: Nigeria actually has a severe shortage of specialized rehab centers, not a surplus. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h7)

question: What is the nurse's role regarding policies for children with special needs?

options.A: Paying for public clinics out of their own salary
options.B: Speaking up for inclusive policies, better buildings, and financial help
options.C: Writing national laws and signing health treaties
options.D: Enforcing tax penalties on families with disabled children

explanation: Nurses act as advocates for their patients to push for better public support and fair treatment. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h7)
